Quick update after a quick calendar sanity check (I tested on G Suite, Outlook Desktop, and Apple Calendar):

  • Outlook Desktop (Windows) sometimes shows the original time with the recipient's local DST rules applied, which can flip the date for recipients in CET during the one-week mismatch.
  • Google Calendar tends to present the correct local wall-clock (it converts correctly to 14:00 CET for Mar 12).
  • Apple Calendar on older macOS versions has had edge-case bugs previously but looks OK on our test machines.

Recommendation: avoid the DST overlap week if the audience will use mixed clients and date fidelity matters. If procurement needs momentum and APAC can accept 21:00 SGT finish time, we can proceed with Thu Mar 12 at 08:00 EST but include explicit date/time language in the invite and add a short line to the invite: "All times shown are in UTC and local timezone — if you see a different date please refer to UTC: 13:00 UTC / 14:00 CET / 21:00 SGT".

If you want my vote: pick Mon Mar 16 09:30 EST (cleaner, fewer client surprises). I'm available both days.
